Theme Description: Recurring focus on overall stance and limb proportions, contrasting bipedal and quadrupedal body plans and detailing forelimb length and configuration.

Subthemes.Subtheme Description: Identifications of two-legged stance and associated cues.
Identifications of four-legged stance and associated cues.
Observations of arm length and robustness relative to body plan.

Theme Description: Descriptions centered on head region, including mouth form, gape, teeth, jaw definition, and sensory features like eyes and nostrils.

Subthemes.Subtheme Description: Shape and capacity of the mouth and beak-like qualities.
Tooth size and visibility, and jaw definition compared across specimens.
Attention to nostrils and eyes, and overall head size cues.

Theme Description: Systematic noting of neck length/posture and tail length/curvature as key body plan markers.

Subthemes.Subtheme Description: Length, thickness, curvature, and consistency of the tail.
Length and posture of the neck, including arched profiles.

Theme Description: Color observations, confidence in color accuracy, and description of stripes, spots, scales, and textural look.

Subthemes.Subtheme Description: Base colors, contrasts, and uncertainty about color accuracy.
Stripes, spots, scale mentions, and rough/wrinkled or spiky-looking textures.

Theme Description: Judgments of absolute and relative size and overall body robustness versus leanness.

Subthemes.Subtheme Description: Small–medium to very large appraisals and length comparisons.
Perceptions of being lean, thick, fat, wider, or elongated, including local limb robustness.

Theme Description: Inferences about herbivory versus carnivory and hypotheses about functional anatomy and performance.

Subthemes.Subtheme Description: Attributions of plant eating based on mouth shape, neck, and overall appearance.
Attributions of meat eating and use of sharp teeth and talons as weapons.
Hypotheses about balance, hand use, crest or spike functions, and foraging mechanics.

Theme Description: Use of animal analogies and references to toys, movies, and personal exposures to make sense of dinosaurs.

Subthemes.Subtheme Description: Comparisons to familiar animals and known dinosaurs to frame interpretation.
Influence of movies, toys, and personal sightings on perceived familiarity.

Theme Description: A systematic approach to noticing body-plan diagnostics first (limbs, head, tail), with coloration treated as secondary.

Subthemes.Subtheme Description: Initial attention to leg count, stance, and forelimb reduction.
Rapid shift to head size and mouth form as distinguishing cues.
Attention to tail length/consistency and overall elongation.
Color noted but considered last and with uncertainty.

Theme Description: Expressed confusion, unfamiliarity, and open questions about identification, relatedness, and evolutionary change.

Subthemes.Subtheme Description: Noting confusion between specimens and uncertainty about correctness and color.
Questioning relationships and pathways of evolutionary change and trait functions.

Theme Description: Attention to spikes, plates, and cranial ornaments, including speculation about their functions.

Subthemes.Subtheme Description: Back spikes/rows and plate-like, spiky-looking features.
Nasal/cranial ornaments and fan-like mouth structures considered as displays.

Theme Description: Detailed focus on distal appendages, including claws, toes, hoof-like structures, and special hooks/spurs.

Subthemes.Subtheme Description: Recognition and characterization of claws, toes, nail thickness, and hoof-like traits.
Identification of a posterior foot hook/spur and its perceived significance.

Theme Description: Emotional reactions to appearance, including judgments of cuteness, scariness, and perceived novelty.

Subthemes.Subtheme Description: Valence judgments ranging from cute to scary.
Perceived familiarity, resemblance to known forms, and uncertainty about identity.

Theme Description: Codes that do not clearly align with any emergent theme.
